A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe HRAvatar and include Appendices A–E. Pages 2–18 have identical text, PDF content, resources and rendered appearance; first-page differences concern affiliation and version markings.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original reconstruction evaluations, ablations, FLARE comparisons and rendering-speed measurements.

after.justification: The same original experimental results remain in Section 4 and Appendix C, including quantitative benchmarks and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain identical expression tracking, learnable blendshapes and skinning, appearance decomposition, shading, losses and optimization procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 10 INSTA, 8 HDTF and 5 self-captured subjects. Self-reenactment, cross-reenactment, relighting, material editing and novel-view demonstrations are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator participation is unchanged across corresponding experiments: INSTA, Point-avatar, Splatting-avatar, Flash-avatar, GBS and FLARE retain their respective main-text and appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain 512 x 512 images, 15 training epochs, the same last-350/500-frame test splits, metrics and baseline controls. Appendix material, geometry and rendering-speed evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same deformation, expression-encoder, shading, normal-loss and albedo-loss ablations. Appendix C.3 already contains the jaw-pose regularization ablation in both versions.

E5.justification: Dataset averages and per-subject reporting are identical. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results match, including appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains HRAvatar PSNR values of 30.36, 28.55 and 28.97 for INSTA, HDTF and self-captured data, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations 1–17 and their associated mathematical explanations are unchanged, including deformation definitions, shading equations and Appendix B.4's BRDF and SplitSum derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning reconstruction quality, precise tracking, flexible deformation, realistic relighting and real-time rendering.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical. Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same qualifications concerning FLAME priors, material-lighting entanglement, full-head reconstruction and possible future improvements.

D1.justification: Implementation, initialization, learning rates, loss weights, hardware, training-time information and environment-map processing instructions are unchanged. Project-page and other access links also retain identical targets.

R1.justification: The 82 references, Section 2's related-work discussion and Appendix E.1's positioning against FLARE, GBS and other avatar methods are identical.

P1.justification: Kangjie Chen's affiliation marker changes from 2 (IDEA) to 1 (Tsinghua University). The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; prose, terminology and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–7 retain identical content, captions, structure and placement. The affiliation and version-text updates do not alter the page layout.

improvement.justification: The revision changes an affiliation marker and version/date information only. Scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility information remain identical, so there is no meaningful overall quality difference.
